These features are more typical of aggressive IDH-wildtype diffuse astrocytic glioma than of many IDH-mutant gliomas. Features arguing against IDH-wildtype include cortical temporal involvement, absence of deep white matter invasion, absence of ependymal invasion, no midline shift, and only a small necrotic proportion, which can be seen in IDH-mutant tumors. On balance, the enhancement/edema pattern and age outweigh the contradictory lower-infiltration features, so the best estimate is IDH-wildtype.

overall_comment: MRI metadata favor an aggressive enhancing adult-type diffuse glioma. Molecular classification cannot be determined definitively from these fields alone; DWI/ADC, perfusion, spectroscopy, susceptibility/calcification assessment, histology, and molecular testing would materially affect certainty. The integrated diagnosis is therefore a best MRI-based estimate, not a substitute for tissue diagnosis.
